name: how a tick scales with the size of the crowd

steps.note: the simulation alone: no frames, no sprites, just process_pass
a hundred, which is where the earlier prototype fell over
ten times the crowd should be about ten times the work
...and so should ten times that, which is where an n^2 becomes obvious
dogs animate and turn, so they are worth measuring separately
the assertion that matters: cost per entity must not grow with the crowd
a hundred entities fit in cache and a thousand do not, so this pair has a
real 1.3-1.8x spread between runs that is not a regression - a quadratic
would be 10x here, so the wide slack still catches the thing being watched
past that the crowd is already out of cache, so this pair is the tight one
a wall well above what this machine does, to catch an order of magnitude
4000 wandering humans is a 0.04ms tick on an M3 in a debug build
the crowd is still all there, and the world it ran in is untouched
